title: Instinct is the AI assistant Silicon Valley can't stop talking about
excerpt: I tried Instinct, the viral AI assistant that books appointments, handles customer service, cancels subscriptions, and more.
content_html:
This AI assistant bought me whey protein and booked a cabin for my birthday

By Pranav Dixit

You're currently following this author! Want to unfollow? Unsubscribe via the link in your email.

Here's everything that Instinct — an invitation-only AI assistant going viral among Silicon Valley tech types — has done for me over the past few days:

• Booked a cabin for my birthday and made a dinner reservation.

• Ordered whey protein from Costco.

• Faxed (faxed!) an obscure document to my bank so I could get a late-fee refund.

• Checked whether a new dentist was in-network and made an appointment.

• Dealt with a human customer service representative at my insurance company.

• Canceled several recurring subscriptions I'd forgotten about.

• Responded to my emails.

Honestly, this service is nuts. And sure, AI tools like OpenClaw, Codex, and Claude Code can already do some of these things. But what makes Instinct different is that it lives in your text messages. There's nothing to set up, and no technical fiddling. You send it a text, and it gets to work.

VCs see the magic, too. The WSJ reported that Instinct is raising $250 million at a $2.5 billion valuation. Its founder, Noah Shinn, is a 23-year-old Northeastern University dropout and an early employee at AI company Sierra. Shinn did not respond to multiple requests for comment.

Instinct is part of Silicon Valley's next big bet: that AI should stop telling us how to do things and just start doing them for us, something that the industry calls "agentic AI." My colleague Hugh Langley reported that Meta is testing something similar called Hatch.

There is, naturally, a catch. An assistant cannot run your life without gaining access to a lot of it. The more hooks that you let Instinct sink into your digital life by connecting it to your email, calendar, and anything else that requires you to log in, the more useful it is. Its terms of service also allow it to train its models on user data. Shinn did not respond to multiple requests for comment.

So here's the part where I should tell you to tread with caution. Instead, I'm just going to leave you with an invitation to sign up. Write to me and tell me the craziest thing you tried.

Pranav Dixit 是《商业内幕》驻旧金山湾区的元记者。 他撰写了有关 Meta 的产品、政策和内部运作的文章，同时研究了该公司的决策如何影响数十亿人的联系和沟通方式。 此前，Pranav 是 BuzzFeed News 驻印度的技术记者，报道硅谷最大的公司对南亚超过 10 亿人的文化、社会和政治的影响。 他还曾担任 Engadget 的高级新闻编辑，并在印度最大的全国性报纸之一《印度斯坦时报》上进行科技报道。普拉纳夫的报道揭示了大型科技公司在新兴市场寻求增长对人类造成的后果，并引发了关于美国科技公司对全球南方影响的广泛讨论。 2019 年，他凭借一部关于 WhatsApp 错误信息如何在印度农村引发可怕私刑的实地专题报道，获得了锡拉丘兹大学的《镜报》奖。 他还从不稳定的地缘政治热点克什米尔进行报道，记录了世界上持续时间最长的互联网关闭。他的作品被主要国内和国际出版物广泛引用，并且他曾在 BBC、半岛电视台和 Vox Media 的 Land of the Giants 等播客上讨论他的作品。 他还在新闻课程中发表过演讲，包括加州大学伯克利分校的研究生新闻课程。 他的文章曾发表在《卫报》、《Vox》、《时代》、《信息》和半岛电视台上。Pranav 于 2021 年从印度新德里移居美国，成为哈佛大学尼曼新闻基金会的研究员，在那里他研究了美国科技媒体的演变以及世界各地的新闻编辑室如何更有效地报道技术和社会。有关于 Meta 或硅谷其他任何地方的建议吗？ 通过加密消息应用程序 Signal (+1408-905-9124) 联系 Pranav，或发送电子邮件至 pdixit@insider.com 或 pranavdixit@protonmail.com。 您还可以通过 WhatsApp +857-753-3949 联系他，或者通过 X (@PranavDixit) 或 BlueSky (@pranavdixit.bsky.social) 与他联系。Pranav 对消息来源保持匿名。 请使用非工作设备进行联系。专业知识：Meta、Facebook、WhatsApp、Llama、AI、Threads、Instagram、马克·扎克伯格、社交媒体、平台、移民
